reporting-back-after-the-revelations-dia.text: Your work in the library, is it done?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-dia.speaker: Lord Ieuan Amlodd
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-dia.text: Then you should speak with Arianwyn at once.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-dia.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-dia.text: I see... You should tell Arianwyn.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-dia.speaker: Elena
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-dia.text: Hey [player name]. You'd better speak with Arianwyn if you're done in the library.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: [player name], you have returned. Did you discover anything in the Grand Library?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.player: I did. I think we should call the others.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: I see. I will summon them at once.
Arianwyn calls the others to the meeting.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Okay, thank you all for joining us. In case you weren't aware, [player name] here has returned from the Grand Library with some news for us.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ilfeen
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: So what happened?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.player: I entered the library and found the seal broken by Lord Iorwerth.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Islwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: So he did break one of the seals. Did it hide anything notable?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.player: Yes, it contained a memory, left behind by Seren herself.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Eluned
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: A memory of Seren? Amazing!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.player: It was only part of something larger though. I had to break the other eight seals to uncover the rest of it.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: So you managed to break all of Seren's seals? Very impressive [player name]. Now tell us, this memory, what was it?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.player: That's where it gets interesting... The memory spoke of a curse on the elves, a curse that Seren was desperately trying to break.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Islwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: A curse? What curse?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.player: A curse binding the elves to Seren. As long as she remained close, it was unnoticeable, but if she went too far... pain, and death.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ysgawyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: But who was responsible? Who cursed our people?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.player: That's the thing... It was Seren herself.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: What?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ysgawyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Seren was our goddess, she would never curse us. How dare you suggest otherwise!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ysgawyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Truth? You don't know the meaning of the word!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Let them finish Ysgawyn!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.player: She didn't mean to do it, she was trying to help. She was using her own essence to try and extend your lifespans, it just went wrong...

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Islwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: I... I don't believe it. She cursed us? Our goddess cursed us?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: If... If what you say is true, how does it relate to Lord Iorwerth's claims?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.player: Seren went to great lengths to undo the curse. She believed that she could nullify it by creating a being of darkness, one to counter her light essence.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Eluned
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: You don't mean...

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.player: Lord Iorwerth spoke the truth. She created a fragment of herself, filled with darkness, hoping to use it to break the curse. It didn't work though, so she sealed it in the Temple of Light.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ilfeen
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: I... I don't...

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Islwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: This can't be real... This is a dream... Tell me this isn't real!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ysgawyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: This is a lie! It has to be! The human is showing their true colours once again!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Lady Tangwen Trahaearn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Boy, what did I tell you about insulting the human!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Eluned
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Arianwyn? What do we do?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Eluned
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Arianwyn?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ysgawyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Why are we still stood here? This human needs putting in chains!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Eluned
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Arianwyn? Do something!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: I... I don't...

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Eluned
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Arianwyn!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: I don't know what to do!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: I don't know what to do...

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: You think I know something you all don't? You think I have some trick hidden up my sleeve? I have nothing!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ysgawyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: You're our leader! Lead!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: And how would you have me do that, Ysgawyn? How am I meant to respond to this?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ysgawyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: You can start by locking this human up. They are a traitor! The curse is clearly a lie!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ysgawyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: If we were truly tied to Seren, we'd have all dropped dead when she was shattered! The curse clearly doesn't exist!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Well... Don't be so sure of that.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ysgawyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Nice of you to suddenly speak up! I'd have thought a king would command a bit of authority rather than crying in the corner!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: I'm not a king any more...

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ysgawyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Well thank Seren for that! You only managed to lose the entire kingdom to Lord Iorwerth!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Islwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: You should learn some respect!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ysgawyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: I have respect! I respect the heroes who died in this war, not the coward that ran away from it!

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: You... You're right. I failed you, I failed you all. I wish I could go back and change that, but I can't. All I can do now, is try and make things right.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: While horrifying, I believe [player name] speaks the truth. They have no reason to lie to us, and what they say does make sense.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Islwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: How?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Most of you never met Seren. You only know her through the stories passed down to you. But I did know her, and I know she was filled with pain.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ilfeen
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: You... You think this is the reason?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: I think it could be. As for why we don't feel the effects of the curse now, that is because Seren is still with us, every one of us.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Eluned
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Of course, the crystal seeds. All of us carry them in some form or other, and all of them came from Seren when she shattered herself.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Her last attempt to break the curse, after everything else failed...

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ilfeen
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: So what do we do?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.player: There's one other thing. Seren built a second set of defences within the Temple of Light, this fragment of her is sealed within them. There's an orb that can bypass these defences.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Islwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: An orb?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.player: Yes, apparently she hid it somewhere called Gorlah.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: I know of Gorlah. It's an old shrine north of Prifddinas, a place for quiet worship away from the city.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ilfeen
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Does Lord Iorwerth know about the orb?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Eluned
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Then he might already have claimed it. We should send someone to check.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ysgawyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: I will go. I wish to see some actual proof of what this human claims.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Islwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: That's not your call. Arianwyn is in charge here.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Am I? My whole life, I've been fighting Lord Iorwerth. My whole life, I've believed him to be a servant of Zamorak. Now I learn that everything I fought for was a lie.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: I don't even know what I'm leading any more...

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Ilfeen
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Maybe Lord Iorwerth fights for a different cause to what we thought, but that doesn't change who he is, that doesn't change what he's done.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: I need time alone... Time to think... Baxtorian, I would appreciate it if you could take charge for a while.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Oh... I... I'll do my best.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: That's all I ask. Now, I would like to be alone.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Eluned
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: You're not the only one. I think we all need time to process this.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-the.text: Then let us close this meeting. We will reconvene later.
The others leave the meeting.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.player: So what do we do now?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.text: There's a lot to think about, for all of us. There's also a lot we still don't know.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.player: Do you think Arianwyn will be okay?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.text: I hope so... I know the pain he feels, it can tear you apart if you're not careful.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.player: You seem to be dealing with it okay.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.text: I'm glad it seems that way, that's not how it feels though. I knew of Seren's troubles, but to know the cause... it's heart-breaking.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.text: Now I find myself leading once more, something I swore I would never do again.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.player: Arianwyn seems to think you're capable.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.text: Yes... But Arianwyn doesn't know me, not really.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.text: Anyway, I suppose my job now is to make sure we don't lose sight of our goal.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.player: Do we know what that is anymore?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.text: To stop Lord Iorwerth. Even if we now know his true intentions, even if some think those intentions may be good, we can't ignore his actions.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.text: He'd see us all dead just to free this fragment of Seren. He has to be stopped.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.player: What do you need me to do?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.text: Ysgawyn has gone to see if he can find the orb you spoke of. No one actually gave him permission, but he seems to care little for orders at the moment.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.text: Once he gets back we'll know more about what to do next. In the meantime, I've managed to decipher the clues left behind by Lord Crwys and Lady Hefin, two more of the clan elders. We should try to find them.

options.text: How do I find Lord Crwys?

steps.player: How do I find Lord Crwys?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Here is the clue he left behind: 'The trees of my home will call to me.'

steps.player: I see, anything else I should know?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: The Crwys clan is a clan of woodcutters and farmers. The entire clan is close to nature, but none more than Lord Crwys.

options.text: How do I find Lady Hefin?

steps.player: How do I find Lady Hefin?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Here is the clue she left behind: 'I will walk across the water to the south.'

steps.player: I see, anything else I should know?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: The Hefin clan are our religious leaders. They teach us to better ourselves, not just in mind, but in body as well. Lady Hefin used to lead some of the more vigorous training exercises of the Hefin clan.

options.text: I'd like to ask you something about yourself.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.player: What do I need to do again?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.speaker: Baxtorian
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-tal.text: You should try and find Lord Crwys and Lady Hefin. They could be of big help to us in the fight against Lord Iorwerth.

options.text: How do I find Lord Crwys?
How do I find Lady Hefin?
I'd like to ask you something about yourself.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.speaker: Lord Piquan Crwys
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.text: A tree? No of course not! I am an elf, but through deep magic, I took on the form of a tree. It allowed me to hide, to stay safe.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.player: Yes. You must be Lord Crwys, Baxtorian sent me to find you. We need your help.
The village of Lletya. It's east of here.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.speaker: Lord Piquan Crwys
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.text: Then it is time for me to uproot. I will head there at once.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.speaker: Lord Piquan Crwys
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.text: It's strange to be an elf again. I spent so long living as a tree I almost forgot what my true form felt like.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.player: Maybe the tree was your true form and this is just your disguise.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.speaker: Lord Piquan Crwys
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.text: Hmmm. Now there's an interesting thought...

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.speaker: Elf Hermit
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.text: A traveller? It's been a long time since I've had any company on this little island of mine.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.speaker: Elf Hermit
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.text: I fear you are at a dead end though, there's nothing of interest for you here.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.player: Don't be so sure. I got here by following a clue, a clue left behind by Lady Hefin. I seek her on behalf of Baxtorian himself.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.speaker: Lady Carys Hefin
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.text: Baxtorian? I see. Then I have good news for you human, you have found the one you seek.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.speaker: Lady Carys Hefin
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.text: I am. I have lived here in solitude for a long time, but now that solitude must end. Where am I needed?

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.player: The village of Lletya, north of here.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.speaker: Lady Carys Hefin
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.text: Then it is time to resume my role among the elves. I will go at once.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.speaker: Lady Carys Hefin
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.text: The road to enlightenment is a perilous one. The latest peril is the largest I've ever seen though.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.player: Do you think we can overcome it.

reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.speaker: Lady Carys Hefin
reporting-back-after-the-revelations-fin.text: That is not for me to say. All I can do is see where this path takes me. And if this is the final step of my journey, then I go to my end willingly.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Oh... Hello. Good work finding Lord Crwys and Lady Hefin. I never thought I'd see the other elders again, maybe we'll have a chance with them alongside us.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.player: No problem. Any news from Ysgawyn?

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: He has just returned. Let us gather the others and hear what he has to say.
Baxtorian calls the others to the meeting.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Now that Ysgawyn has returned, I thought we should gather to hear what he has discovered.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Eluned
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Where is Arianwyn?

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Elena
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: I saw him heading out into the forest earlier. He must have wanted some time alone.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Eluned
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: I hope he's okay.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: He'll be alright, just give him time. While he is gone, we need to keep making progress.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: On that note, what news do you have, Ysgawyn?

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: The shrine at Gorlah was empty. The orb was removed quite a while ago by the looks of things.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.player: So do you believe me now?

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: If it helps with your overinflated ego, then yes, I now believe you.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Islwyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: If the orb isn't at Gorlah, Lord Iorwerth must have claimed it. It could be anywhere now.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Well luckily for us, I know exactly where it is. There's a cave just north of the Iorwerth Camp that is used to store supplies. Lord Iorwerth has it under close guard there.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ilfeen
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: How do you know this?

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Because I went scouting.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Scouting? At the Iorwerth Camp? Who gave you permission?

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: I gave myself permission. I do not serve you, Baxtorian, or anyone else here.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Islwyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: No, you just serve yourself, don't you Ysgawyn?

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: My actions benefit us all! Now that we know where the orb is, we can move to claim it.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Eluned
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: But why would Lord Iorwerth keep the orb at the camp? Surely it would be more secure behind the Prifddinas walls.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: That's the other thing I found out. Lord Iorwerth knows we managed to enter the library. He fears the orb would not be safe behind the walls.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: How did you discover this?

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: I have my methods...

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: It worries me that you are unwilling to share them.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Save your suspicions for someone who cares.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ilfeen
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: So we know where the orb is. What do we do now?

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Lord Iorwerth intends to use the orb to free the dark fragment of Seren. We need to stop him.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Eluned
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: But this fragment of Seren, it's still part of her. Lord Iorwerth has done some unspeakable things, but he doesn't serve Zamorak like we thought, maybe we can reason with him.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: I tried to reason with Lord Iorwerth a long time ago... It won't work, as much as I wish it would.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Regardless of his intentions, Lord Iorwerth is our enemy. You should want to kill him, not reason with him.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: I would never wish for the death of a fellow elf, no matter what they've done.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Well look at you with your moral high ground.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Now is not the time for arguing. At some point, we will need to decide what to do about the fragment of Seren. For now though, we need to focus on getting that orb and stopping Lord Iorwerth.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Islwyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: The orb isn't enough for him to win though, he'll also need to break through the defences on the Temple of Light. He'll struggle to do that now he's lost Ardougne.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.player: There is another way into the temple though, a tunnel from the Underground Pass, built by the dwarves there.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Great... Dwarves... I hate dwarves.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Islwyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: You hate everything Ysgawyn.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Lord Iorwerth will stop at nothing to enter the temple. We have to assume that sooner or later, he will find that tunnel.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Lady Carys Hefin
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Then we should make sure the tunnel is secure. Baxtorian, allow myself and the other elders to go meet with these dwarves.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Very well, head to the Underground Pass and see what you can do. In the meantime, we should secure that orb. Even if he does get into the temple, Lord Iorwerth can do nothing without it.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Let me guess, you're going to send your favourite human.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Islwyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Jealous, Ysgawyn?

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: No. I have other things to do anyway.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Baxtorian
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: [player name], head to the cave at the Iorwerth Camp and recover the Orb of Light. Be careful though, it's likely to be well guarded.

recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.speaker: Islwyn
recovering-the-orb-ysgawyn-returns.text: Sounds like we're done here. Let's get moving.

recovering-the-orb-talking-to-baxtorian-.speaker: Baxtorian

recovering-the-orb-talking-to-baxtorian-.speaker: Baxtorian

recovering-the-orb-confronting-ysgawyn.speaker: Ysgawyn
recovering-the-orb-confronting-ysgawyn.text: Lord Iorwerth took everything from me! My whole life was destroyed by him and that dog, Essyllt! Do you really think I'd join up with them?

recovering-the-orb-confronting-ysgawyn.text: Not to mention the fact that it kept Iestin safe from any informants that Lord Iorwerth might have among the rebels.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Go! I'll get Mawrth and the other citizens to safety!

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Well well, the great King Baxtorian. I wasn't sure I believed it when I heard you were still alive, but here you are.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I'm sorry to disappoint you.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Well your ability to disappoint is one of your few talents, so I'll let it slide. However, I must insist that you give me the orb.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Ysgawyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Crawl back into the hole you came from Lord Iorwerth, you won't leave here with that orb!

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Oh I will, one way or another. But in case it wasn't clear, let me explain the situation.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: As we speak, my forces are dealing with the last of your rebels and rounding up your citizens. You have no way to fight, and nowhere to run.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Of course, I could just have you all killed right now. After the trouble you've all caused me, it wouldn't be an unreasonable act. However, I am not without mercy, and I will not draw blood unless I have to.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Instead, I give you a choice. Give me the orb, and I will withdraw my forces, leaving you in peace. Refuse, and the blood of those citizens will be on your hands.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Islwyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: We do not barter with your kind!

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I feared as much. That said, I do have someone here who might change your mind.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Islwyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Arianwyn!

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Ysgawyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: What is this? What have you done?

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: What have I done? Well I told him the truth. It was about time that someone did.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Islwyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: What truth?

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: They're not the enemy. I thought they were, for so long, but they're not.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Everything we have done, every sacrifice we have made, all of it has been to free our goddess.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: You've never sacrificed, you've never lost anything. You only sacrifice those around you...

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: You have some nerve to lecture me. Remind me, how many of your people died under your watch? How many fell, trying to free your wife?

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: These new followers of yours, do they know? Do they know what you did? Do they know about the monster you truly are?

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I never...

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: No... of course they don't. You're a liar and a coward, that's all you've ever been.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: As for me, I'm many things, and I admit, a lot of them aren't good. But I would never throw lives away like you did.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Islwyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: What's he on about?

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Nothing... He's lying. He's just trying to justify his mistakes.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I've done many terrible things, but none of them were a mistake. Every sacrifice I've made has been for her, for Seren.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Ysgawyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: And what are these apparent sacrifices you've made? Nothing compared to the suffering you've caused me, I'm sure!

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: When I first discovered the truth, our clan was still ruled by my mother. I went to her, told her what I'd found, told her what we needed to do.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I loved my mother, but she was blindly loyal to this fool here, she wouldn't have any of it. I couldn't just abandon my goddess though, she needed us. So I did what had to be done.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: You killed her?

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: And I would do it again without hesitation. For Seren, there is no price too great.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Islwyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: You're a monster! Surely you don't mean to side with this barbarian, Arianwyn.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I don't condone what he did, what any of them have done. But they want what we want, we have to try working together.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Ysgawyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I'll die before working with them.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: No one else needs to die here. Please, just give me the orb. Do that, and I swear we will do you no further harm.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I... I can't.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I see. I did hope it wouldn't come to this, but you've given me no choice. Morvran.
Morvran leaves, bringing Eoin in.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Eoin
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: What's going on? Where's mummy?

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I'll make this simple for you, Baxtorian. The life of the boy is now in your hands. Give me the orb, and no harm will come to him.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: You wouldn't...

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: No, I wouldn't. But the choice is not mine, it's yours. I will count to five.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: One.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Lord Iorwerth, please...

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Two.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Baxtorian, please. Just give him the orb.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Three.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Eoin
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I don't like this, I want mummy!

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Four.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Stop!

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I'll give you the orb. Just please, don't hurt anyone else.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: A wise choice, must be a first for you.
Baxtorian gives Lord Iorwerth the orb.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Ysgawyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: No!
Ysgawyn attempts to stop them, but Essylt kills him in one hit.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Islwyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Ysgawyn!

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Islwyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Get after them!

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: It wasn't meant to go like this. No one was meant to get hurt. I'm sorry.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: For so long I was led to believe that Lord Iorwerth was our enemy. I thought he'd turned his back on Seren, thought he'd betrayed her.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: But I was wrong. Everything we thought we were fighting for was a lie. He never betrayed her, everything he did was to free her.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.player: Whatever it is he's trying to free... it isn't her.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: How do you know? Because of what you found in the library? How do we know that was her? How do we know what's true anymore?

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.player: So that's why you turned to Lord Iorwerth? To find out the truth?

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: My whole life I've dreamed of her, dreamed of what it would be like to meet her. If there's even a chance that she's still alive, I have to know.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.player: And if she is alive? Then what?

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: Seren guided the elves for thousands of years. With her back, we'll finally be able to reform Prifddinas. We'll finally have peace again.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.player: Peace? Look around you Arianwyn. Look at what Lord Iorwerth has done to this village, your home. Does this look like the work of someone who wants peace?
It doesn't have to be this way. Step aside. Let me stop Lord Iorwerth and reclaim the orb. Once he's dealt with, we can find out the truth, our way.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: You... you know I can't do that.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: I'm sorry friend, but I've made my choice. Now please, walk away. No one else needs to die here.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.player: I can't let him get away.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: And I can't let you go after him.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Ysgawyn...

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: He wasn't a friend, to any of us. Everything he cared about he lost a long time ago.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: But he didn't give up. To the very end, he fought for a cause he believed in, our cause.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: And now he's gone. Along with the orb and that traitor, Arianwyn. Lord Iorwerth has everything he needs now. He'll be preparing to move on the temple as we speak.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Ilfeen
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: We can't give up Islwyn. If we do, then he died for nothing.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Oh I don't intend to give up, but make no mistake, this is a fight we're unlikely to win.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Eluned
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: So what do we do? Baxtorian?

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: I... I don't think there's anything we can do. Lord Iorwerth will destroy us if we try to stop him.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Maybe, but we have to try. What else is there?

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: We'd be throwing lives away...

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Well Lord Iorwerth seemed to think you were no stranger to that. Why did he think that?

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: I don't know, probably just some lie he tells himself.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Hmm. I don't believe you.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: You'd trust Lord Iorwerth over me?

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: I wouldn't trust Lord Iorwerth if my life depended on it. I know a liar when I see one though, and I can tell you're not being honest about something.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: What happened? Tell us.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: It was after we were defeated by Lord Iorwerth. With Prifddinas lost to us, we returned to our kingdom in the east. We'd been gone for years by then, and in our absence, the kingdom had fallen to our other foes.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: So many dead... my people, the ones I was meant to protect. But that wasn't the worst of it. Glarial, my beloved, she was taken from me.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: We searched far and wide, desperate to find her. At times it felt like we were close, but the enemy always managed to elude us.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Eventually, we managed to track her captors to some caves south of our ruined kingdom. It was clearly a trap, but I was a fool. I was so blind in my desire to find her, I didn't consider the obvious.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: I sent my soldiers in, the few that I still had. They fought the best they could, but it was hopeless. They were massacred.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: After that, I knew I couldn't carry on. I was alone and powerless. So I sealed myself away, in the hope that one day she would come back to me.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: You... you killed them? You killed them all?

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: I did. But you don't understand, I loved my wife. If there was a chance of freeing her, I had to take it.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: You think I don't understand love? I knew love, for Eirlys! My mother! Your daughter! She died in your war, while you hid away!

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Lord Iorwerth was right! You're just a coward!

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Eluned
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Islwyn, where are you going?

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: The Underground Pass! I intend to fight for my people, even if their own king won't!
Islwyn leaves, and the funeral ends.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: I used to think I was a good king, one that took care of his people. Thanks to me, they had roofs over their heads and food for their tables.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: And yet... I never loved them, not really. The only thing I loved was her, my Glarial.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: When they took her from me... I was torn apart. I vowed I would get her back no matter the cost. That vow destroyed my people... I destroyed my people. In the end... I became just like Lord Iorwerth.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: Maybe you did fail your people, you didn't destroy them though.
You think this is over? Is that it? Lord Iorwerth beats us once so we just give up? If you truly think that then yes, you have destroyed your people!
Do you want to just rot here? Wallowing in your own self pity while you lose the little you still have?
We can fight! Lord Iorwerth doesn't win until he gets into the Temple of Light! We can still stop this!

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: But he outnumbers us ten to one... We'll all die.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: Surely it's better to die trying than to live a life of regret? I'd have thought you'd know that better than anyone.

Oh for crying out loud! You have got to be the biggest waste of space I have ever met! I've met goblins with more of a spine than you! For once in your miserable life why don't you actually do something worthwhile?

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: You... You're awful at pep talks.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: It wasn't meant to be a pep talk!
sigh* Look... Ask yourself this... What would she want?

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: She... She'd want me to save them.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: Then why are we still stood around talking? We've got work to do!

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: I... You're right... We don't have a plan though.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: Lord Iorwerth only has one way into the Temple of Light, the dwarf tunnel from the Underground Pass. We need to stop him getting through.
The dwarves should be able to seal the tunnel. We'll need to defend them while they do.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: But we don't have the strength to withstand Lord Iorwerth's forces.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: We have the clan elders, their combined power is an army in itself.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: Not all the clan elders. We're still missing two.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: Well have you deciphered their clues?

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: I have, but there's a problem. We should hopefully be able to find Lady Meilyr. But Lady Ithell, she died in the early days of the war.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: That's not good. Did she have any descendants?

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: I had a look. Kelyn Ithell is her closest living relative. Problem is, we don't just need a Lady Ithell, we need the Lady Ithell.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: An illness of some sort, I never actually knew what it was. She'd had it for years.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: For years? So she'd have been ill when she gave you her clue. If she knew she was dying, maybe her clue reflects that.
Knowledge can be passed on. Maybe the clue will lead us to her knowledge.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: I... I suppose you could be right.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: It's worth a shot at least. Leave it with me and I'll see what I can do. In the meantime, you should take the others to the dwarf camp in the Underground Pass.
See if you can get in contact with General Hining and the new king of Ardougne as well. Maybe they'll be willing to help us.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: I'll see what I can do. We'll need to work quickly though, Lord Iorwerth will be preparing his forces as we speak. Now I guess you'll be wanting to hear those clues?

steps.player: What's Lady Ithell's clue?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Here is the clue she left behind: 'I'll put my soul into my greatest work.'

steps.player: I see, anything else I should know?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: The Ithell clan is a clan of builders and architects. Before her death, Lady Ithell was considered the finest architect of all the elves. This village was her final and finest contribution to our people.

steps.player: What's Lady Meilyr's clue?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Here is the clue she left behind: 'Follow the scrolls to find me.'

steps.player: I see, anything else I should know?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: The Meilyr clan is a clan of scientists and explorers. You'll probably need to do some exploring yourself to find Lady Meilyr. You may also find this of use.
If the player has no inventory space:
Baxtorian tries to give you a scroll but you don't have enough room to take it.
If the player has inventory space:
Baxtorian has given you a scroll.

options.text: I'd like to ask you something about yourself.

steps.player: I'll be back later.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian-ta.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian-ta.text: Do you need to hear one of the clues again?

options.text: I'd like to ask you something about yourself.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.speaker: Iestin
after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.text: Well I can't really go back to Lord Iorwerth now. He knows I betrayed him.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.player: No, but you don't have to stay here.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.speaker: Iestin
after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.text: I've made my decision and I intend to stick by it.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.player: So why follow him in the first place?

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.speaker: Iestin
after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.text: After we lost Seren, Baxtorian was chosen to lead us. Rather than looking after the city of Prifddinas, he chose to expand to the east, leaving us behind.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.speaker: Iestin
after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.text: With no ruler, Prifddinas fell into chaos. When Lord Iorwerth came to us and said he'd found a way to bring Seren back to us, you can understand why we turned to him.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.speaker: Iestin
after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.text: I wish things were as simple as good against evil, but that's rarely the case.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.player: I suppose you're right. Anyway, I'd better get going.

after-the-attack-talking-to-elena.player: Hey Elena. What are you up to?

after-the-attack-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
after-the-attack-talking-to-elena.text: Making sure I've got everything ready. I'll be leaving for the Underground Pass soon.

after-the-attack-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
after-the-attack-talking-to-elena.text: Well I've stuck around for this long, it would feel wrong to leave now. Besides, I may not be much of a fighter, but I can help in other ways.

after-the-attack-talking-to-elena.player: Very true. I'll leave you to prepare.

after-the-attack-talking-to-mawrth.speaker: Mawrth
after-the-attack-talking-to-mawrth.text: I can't thank you enough for what you did. My children might be dead if not for you.

after-the-attack-talking-to-mawrth.speaker: Mawrth
after-the-attack-talking-to-mawrth.text: You're a hero and all of us here know it. Again, thank you.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-tou.text: You feel your mind fill with knowledge as the symbol vanishes before you. The knowledge is incomplete though.
The symbol vanishes before you as you gain the final piece of knowledge. The combined knowledge is a design for a statue to be built in the middle of Lletya, requiring 8 Limestone Bricks.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.text: I... I see it! I see everything! All of her knowledge, I have it now!

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.text: Yes, I know everything that she knew! The statue, it must have given it to me somehow!

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.player: You're the closest living relative of Lady Ithell. Now you have her knowledge as well. I suppose that makes you the new Lady Ithell.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.text: I... I suppose it does. Wow!

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.text: I guess you'll be wanting me to help defend the Underground Pass then? Well don't worry, I was planning on joining you anyway. With this new knowledge, I can be an even bigger help.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.text: I'll head there right away. Time is of the essence.
Lady Ithell departs for the Underground Pass.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-meilyr.speaker: Lady Ffion Meilyr
after-the-attack-finding-lady-meilyr.text: At last Baxtorian calls to me. I can't say I expected him to send a human, but I suppose nothing is as expected these days.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-meilyr.player: We need your help. The final fight against Lord Iorwerth is nearly here.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-meilyr.speaker: Lady Ffion Meilyr
after-the-attack-finding-lady-meilyr.text: I will join you in this darkest of hours. Where must I go?

after-the-attack-finding-lady-meilyr.player: The battle will take place in the Underground Pass. Head to Lletya first though, Baxtorian will meet you there.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Oh... Hello. Most of the others have departed for the Underground Pass. I'll be leaving with the rest soon.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Then I shall meet you there.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Don't take too long. We'll be at the dwarf camp.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: How are you Islwyn?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Islwyn
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: As good as can be, all things considered. I idolised my grandfather for years. They always say you should never meet your heroes though, now I see why.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: He's still your family though.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Islwyn
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: He is, he's the only family I have left. The rest of them died in his war. A war that will finally end today.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Islwyn
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Maybe if we both survive, I'll find it in my heart to forgive him. But for now, I have to focus elsewhere.

steps.player: I'll leave you to prepare.

steps.speaker: Islwyn
steps.text: Good luck [player name]. I'll see you on the other side.

options.text: Could I buy some crystal equipment?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Eluned
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Arianwyn is out there, walking alongside our greatest enemy.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Eluned
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: He saved me once you know. Some of Lord Iorwerth's men found me in the forest. There were too many for me to fight off, I thought I was done for. Without Arianwyn, I wouldn't be here today.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Eluned
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: But now he fights alongside them. This war has torn us apart, all of us.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Well it ends today.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Eluned
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Yes, today it ends... For better, or for worse.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Ilfeen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I wonder if Essyllt will join the battle today.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: What will you do if he does?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Ilfeen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Me? Nothing. I'm not much of a fighter. I'll be helping with the wounded instead.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Ilfeen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: You though... If you see him, don't show him mercy, for he will show you none. Instead, you should show him what happens to those who hurt us.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: For Ysgawyn?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Ilfeen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: No one liked him that much, but he was one of us, and he died trying to save us. He deserves justice.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: If I get the chance, I'll make sure he gets it.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Ilfeen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Thank you friend.

steps.player: I'd better get going.

options.text: Could you enchant something for me?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Those are my people coming for us. My brothers and sisters.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: They were once, but not anymore. You're one of us now.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: He's not evil you know, Lord Iorwerth. None of them are really, apart from Essyllt maybe.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Those that follow him, they do so because they believe in him, believe in what he's doing. For a long time, I believed in him as well.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: So why did you betray him?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: He became so obsessed with his cause, he forgot why we started following him in the first place. He became more extreme, more radical.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I tried to advise him as best I could, but over time he started listening more to Essyllt and less to me.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: After I lost my brother, who died following Lord Iorwerth's orders, I realised he needed to be stopped before it was too late.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: You made the right choice.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I hope so. But even now I find myself filled with doubt.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Kamen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Nothing like a *hic* bit of home brew before getting to work.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Are you sure you should be drinking? We can't afford to make mistakes here.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Kamen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Argh, I work better with a bit of *hic* brew in me. Nothing for you to *hic* worry about.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: If you're sure.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Klank
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Didn't think I'd see you back down here [player name]. The elves are lucky to have you on their side.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: They're lucky to have you as well, you're our last hope.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Klank
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: What an awful thought. Four dwarves, one a drunk, are the final hope against this darkness. I hope we don't let you down.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: You won't.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Klank
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I hope you're right friend.

steps.player: Take care Klank.

steps.speaker: Klank
steps.text: You too adventurer...

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Niloof
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: [player name]. We'll soon be ready to seal the tunnel, it's slow work I'm afraid.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: How come?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Niloof
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: If we do this wrong, we'll bring the entire cavern down upon all of us.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Well that would definitely stop Lord Iorwerth.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Niloof
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: It would. I don't know about you though, but I intend to survive this day. Bringing the cavern down isn't a good way to achieve that.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: True that. I'll leave you to your work.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Thorgel
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Hey there [player name].

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: How's it going Thorgel?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Thorgel
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Apart from the army of elves about to descend on us, pretty good.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: You'll be fine, you've got all of us to defend you.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Thorgel
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Well let's hope your better at fighting than Kamen is at brewing, or this will be a short battle.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lord Ieuan Amlodd
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: So here we are. At long last, the end is upon us. The only question that remains is who it's the end for.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: You knew this day would come?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lord Ieuan Amlodd
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: No war lasts forever, not even this one. The darkest verse of the song of the elves is upon us. Who knows what the next verse will be.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Tangwen Trahaearn
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Lord Iorwerth better show up soon! I can't wait forever!

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: You seem keen.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Tangwen Trahaearn
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I've lived for thousands of years. If I'm going to die today, I'd rather just get on with it.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Fair enough.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lord Piquan Crwys
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: This is a dark place we've come to. Fitting I suppose, for this is to be our darkest hour.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Do you think the fragment of Seren is the cause of the darkness?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lord Piquan Crwys
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Possibly, I suspect it was here long before her though. And whatever happens today, I'm sure it will remain for long after.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Carys Hefin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: The greatest battle of our time is almost upon us. We should take the time to reflect.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I've never really been one for looking backwards. I prefer to look ahead.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Carys Hefin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: You can still reflect on the future as well as the past. If we survive today, our future will be changed forever.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I suppose. I'll probably wait until we've won to think about that though.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Carys Hefin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: As you wish.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I hope we win today. It would be a bit embarrassing to be known as the shortest serving clan elder.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I bet. I'd also like to avoid death if possible. I suspect it's not very fun.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Not much is fun when Lord Iorwerth is involved. If all goes well though, he won't be a problem after today.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Ffion Meilyr
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I've been on the run from Lord Iorwerth for centuries. I'll be glad to finally see peace.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: So you think we'll win?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Ffion Meilyr
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Don't forget that death is a form of peace.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I guess. I'd rather avoid it if I can though.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Ffion Meilyr
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: There are worse things in this world than death. Never forget that.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Good to see you General.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: General Hining
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: And you friend. It will be an honour to fight against the darkness alongside you. Together, we can avenge King Tyras.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: You seem well prepared for the battle, compared to the rest of us at least.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: General Hining
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: We knew this battle would come, ever since the day our king died. We've been prepared for a long time.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I hope it's enough.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: General Hining
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: As do I. If it's not though, we'll make sure they remember us until the end of their days.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: That we will.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Ah... You made it.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: That I did. I see you managed to gather some allies.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Yes, General Hining has given us the full support of the Tyras forces. Sadly though, the new king of Ardougne does not wish to assist us.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Typical, after all we did for them.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I suppose they've had enough of elves.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Hmmm. How are the defences looking?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: We've managed to fortify the area around the camp quite well. The dwarves have set up some cannons and General Hining's men have built some catapults.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Good. We may be outnumbered, but the defences will give us a fighting chance.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I hope so... I fear it won't be enough to win though.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: We don't need to win, we just need to buy the dwarves enough time to seal that tunnel. Do we know how long they'll need?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: They haven't given us an exact time, it's a slow process apparently.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Well I suppose we don't want them to do it wrong, they could bring the entire cavern down on top of us. Do we know where Lord Iorwerth is?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: The scouts have reported that his forces are on the move as we speak. It won't be long.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Let's use the time wisely then. Is there anything I can do before the attack begins?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Elena said she had an idea that might help our defence. You could talk to her and see if she needs any help.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I'll get right on it.
What do I need to do again?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Speak with Elena. She said she had an idea that might help our defence.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I'll get right on it.

steps.text: Well I think we can make use of it again. I've combined the alcohol with some other chemicals. The result is quite explosive!
